Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
items.excerpt: Anthropic is releasing Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, its most powerful models to date, in two versions: one freely available and one reserved for verified organizations. The models solve open physics problems, show stronger cybersecurity capabilities, design functioning operating systems, and write more than 90 percent of the changes merged into Anthropic's core code, according to the company. Anthropic says it has deliberately curbed any capabilities that would let the AI accelerate its own development. items.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
items.excerpt: Meta is introducing Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient AI model, optimized for repetitive agent tasks such as tool calls, routing, and data extraction. According to Meta, it delivers more intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna. But it falls short when it comes to actual programming tasks. items.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
items.excerpt: Bytedance Seed has introduced Seedream 5.5, an image model built for professional production workflows. It supports stable multi-pass editing over up to 100 iterations, generates native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds, and, according to Bytedance, outperforms GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst in realism. A Pro version is planned. The article Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Tencent's AI chief says AI bioweapons are coming, but closing off models isn't the answer
items.excerpt: Tencent chief AI scientist Vinces Yao Shunyu warns that AI will soon be able to develop bioweapons and argues for a middle ground between open and closed models. While safety filters on open-source systems can be easily stripped through abliteration, closed models like Anthropic's Claude often block too aggressively. For its upcoming open-weight model Hy4, Tencent is filtering dangerous hacking knowledge directly from the training data.
